items.title: LLMは入力情報が欠損したとき、その欠損の程度に応じてConfidenceを下げられるか？
items.summary:
LLMは入力情報が欠損したとき、その欠損の程度に応じてConfidenceを下げられるか？

→結論：十分に下げられない。ただし、Multi-samplingした回答のEntropyは、欠損による不確実性の増加を比較的よく反映する。

arXiv preprint（2026年5月、NeurIPS 2026 Position Paperとして記載・採択未確認）｜被引用数：0件（ResearchGate掲載値）

背景

オランダのTNO（応用科学研究機構）とユトレヒト大学の統計学研究者Stef van Buurenによる研究。

LLMは入力情報が不足すると、内部知識を使って暗黙的に欠損情報を補完する。統計学の多重代入法と同様に、欠損情報が増えるほど不確実性も増加するべきではないか？

方法

GPT-4o-miniを使用し、SQuADの400問を評価。
参照文書を100%、50%、30%、10%、0%の5段階に削減。
各条件で10回回答を生成（Multi-sampling）。
2つの不確実性指標を比較。
Sampling-based Confidence： 最頻回答の割合（例：10回中8回同じ回答なら80%）。
Response Entropy： 全回答の出現確率分布のばらつき。回答の種類が多く、均等に分散するほど高い。
結果
情報欠損が増えるとAccuracyは大幅に低下するが、Sampling-based Confidenceは十分に低下しない。

Entropyは情報欠損に伴って上昇し、Accuracyの変動をConfidenceよりよく説明した（R²の差は最大0.057）。

ただし、10回すべて同じ誤答を出す場合はEntropyが0になるため、誤った確信を検出できない。
まとめ
入力欠損に対するLLMの不確実性評価には、最頻回答率よりEntropyが有用。ただし、回答が一貫して間違っている場合には限界がある。

Title: LLMs as Implicit Imputers: Uncertainty Should Scale with Missing Information

items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by [...] Many health communicators assume that those who learn the facts will pursue healthier choices. AI is now being built on the same assumption, which ignores how messages actually influence behavior. Messages, like medicines, can help, harm, or do nothing at all, and the only way to know which is to test them.

The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Anthropic and OpenAI are coming for the development workflow | InfoWorld
items.summary: This is clearly where the frontier labs are moving, even though they’ve all benefited from an industry that provided neutral spaces to build. For example, OpenAI developed Pando, a Git back end for its own monorepo, to handle more engineers and agents reading and writing code concurrently. Its engineers kept using Git. That compatibility let it rebuild the back end around the way its engineers [...] This pressure to maximize profitability helps explain why frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are aggressively adding functionality to own more of the developer’s workflow. On November 4, OpenAI announced an agreement to buy Pierre, the company behind Code Storage and the open source libraries Codex already uses to browse files and review changes. OpenAI wants Codex to be where developers work, from the first branch an agent creates through deployment of the application. There’s money in [...] OpenAI or Anthropic could build the place developers prefer to work. The question is what happens when a team likes that place and wants a rival’s agent for a particular job. Maybe a startup has built a tool that can track down the intermittent test failure that’s had the team stumped for a week. Give it access to the code and test history the team has authorized, and it gets a chance to prove itself. Ask the team to move its work to a new platform first, and it probably never gets to try.
